title: Full Mock Exam – All Chapters
description: A comprehensive exam covering all chapters of the FIDE Arbiter's Manual

questions.text: What is the objective of each player in a game of chess?

options.text: To capture all opponent's pieces
To place the opponent's king under attack with no legal escape
To occupy the centre of the board
To promote a pawn to a queen

questions.explanation: As per Article 1.1, the objective of each player is to place the opponent's king under attack in such a way that the opponent has no legal move. This is called checkmate.

questions.text: How must the chessboard be placed at the start of the game?

options.text: Near corner square to the left of each player must be white
Near corner square to the right of each player must be black
Near corner square to the right of each player must be white
It does not matter which way the board is placed

questions.explanation: As per Article 1.2, the near corner square to the right of each player must be white.

questions.text: What happens if a player arrives after the default time at the start of a session?

options.text: The player receives a warning
The player's clock continues to run
The player shall lose the game unless the arbiter decides otherwise
The game is adjourned

questions.explanation: As per Article 6.7, any player who arrives at the chessboard after the start of the session shall lose the game unless the arbiter decides otherwise.

options.text: When a player's king is in check with no legal move
When a player has no legal move and their king is NOT in check
When both players agree to end the game
When only kings remain on the board

questions.explanation: As per Article 9.1, stalemate occurs when the player to move has no legal move and their king is NOT in check. The game is drawn.

questions.text: What is a player forbidden to use during play?

options.text: A scoresheet
Notes, sources of information or advice
A chess clock
A pen or pencil

questions.explanation: As per Article 11.1, during play the players are forbidden to use any notes, sources of information or advice, or analyse on another chessboard.

questions.text: What is the penalty if a player is found to have a mobile phone in the playing venue?

options.text: A warning is issued
Time is added to the opponent's clock
The player shall lose the game; the opponent shall win
The game is restarted

questions.explanation: As per Article 11.2, if a player has a mobile phone on their person in the playing venue, they shall lose the game and the opponent shall win.

questions.text: Can a player leave the playing venue during a game?

options.text: Yes, at any time freely
Yes, but only with permission of the arbiter
No, never under any circumstances
Yes, but only during the opponent's turn

questions.explanation: As per Article 11.5, players may leave the playing venue during the game only with the permission of the arbiter.

questions.text: What is the primary duty of a FIDE Arbiter?

options.text: To assist players with their moves
To see that the Laws of Chess are strictly observed
To record all moves of each game
To broadcast the games to spectators

questions.explanation: As per Article 12.1, the arbiter shall see that the Laws of Chess are strictly observed and act in the best interest of the competition.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a valid penalty an arbiter can apply?

options.text: Warning the player
Declaring the game lost by the offending player
Awarding the offending player extra time
Expulsion from the event

questions.explanation: As per Article 12.2, arbiters increase the OPPONENT's time (not the offender's). Valid penalties: warning, increasing opponent's time, reducing offender's time, declaring loss, expulsion.

questions.text: When should the arbiter intervene in a game?

options.text: Whenever the arbiter believes a player is making a bad move
Only in cases described by the Laws of Chess
Whenever a player requests advice
At the end of every 10 moves

questions.explanation: As per Article 12.7, the arbiter shall not intervene in a game except in cases described by the Laws of Chess.
